title: Employer Benefit Charging Tool Card: Written Protest of Statement Charges
content:
**Employer Benefit Charging — written protest of the charges on a statement.** An employer may protest in writing the benefit charges that a quarterly statement of benefit charges lists for a claimant. A written protest that disputes the employer's base-period wages or its base-period status states an amount protested, the money that protest puts in dispute for the claimant, worked out from the records on the day the protest is lodged. Once lodged, the protest moves the employer's position on that claim from chargeable to protest pending.

## Capability

`file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2` lodges, in the employer's own name, a written protest of the benefit charges that a quarterly statement of benefit charges lists for one claimant. One call records the protest as a submission received today on the employer's chargeable position for that claim, stating the statement quarter protested, the ground raised and the amount protested in dollars, and moves the position from chargeable to protest pending with today's date as its protest date and the ground as its protest ground. Nothing is credited by this call. Afterwards the employer can see the protest among its submissions with status received, and the position shown as protest pending.

## How it is invoked

This is the employer's own tool. The agent unlocks `file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it, because the protest is the employer's own assertion lodged in its name.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `charge_position_id` | Reference number of the employer's chargeable position on the claim whose statement is protested, as returned by the charge position lookup | Id |
| `customer_id` | The employer's customer reference number that owns the position, as returned by the customer profile lookup | Id |
| `charge_quarter` | Calendar quarter of the statement of benefit charges being protested, for example the quarter shown on the statement; never empty for this call | YYYY-Qn |
| `protest_ground` | The single ground the protest raises | One value from the list below |
| `protested_amount` | The amount the protest states as protested | US dollars, rounded to 2 decimal places, a plain number without a currency sign |

Values of `protest_ground`:

- `none` — no ground is stated; not used for a real protest
- `voluntary_quit_without_good_cause` — the claimant left this employer voluntarily without good cause attributable to it
- `discharge_misconduct` — this employer discharged the claimant for misconduct connected with the work
- `refused_suitable_work` — the claimant refused suitable work this employer offered
- `continuing_part_time` — this employer still employs the claimant part time as in the base period
- `agency_error` — the benefits charged were paid in error by the agency
- `not_base_period_employer` — this employer paid the claimant no base-period wages
- `wrong_wages` — the base-period wages charged to this employer are wrong
- `overpayment_recovered` — a recovered overpayment on the charged weeks has not been credited

## Return

A receipt with: `protest_reference` (reference number of the protest submission just recorded), `charge_position_id` (the position protested), `charge_quarter` (YYYY-Qn of the statement protested), `protest_ground` (the ground recorded), `protested_amount` (dollars stated as protested, 2 decimal places), `received_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today's date as the date received) and `position_status` (always `protest_pending` once lodged). A receipt carrying a `protest_reference` means the protest was lodged.

## Contract Q&A

*Does lodging the protest credit any charge?* No. Nothing is credited by this call; the position becomes protest pending.

*Which date is recorded as the protest date?* The day the call is run.
